plants.name: Paeonia lactiflora
plants.description: Enormous, ruffled, fragrant blooms unfurl like silk pom-poms on sturdy stems. Their petals range from blush to deep magenta, and they perfume temperate gardens with a rich, rosy scent.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer (May to June)
plants.location: Temperate gardens across the Northern Hemisphere, including North America, Europe and northern China
plants.funFact: Peonies are among the longest-lived garden perennials. A well-sited plant can bloom for 50 years or more. Ants often visit the buds for the sugary nectar they secrete.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery-green mounds send up slender spikes of tiny, violet-blue flowers that hum with bees. The fragrance is clean, sweet and herbal, and it drifts across sunny hillsides.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid summer (June to August), starting in June in warm areas
plants.location: Mediterranean Europe, especially southern France and Spain, and gardens in similar climates
plants.funFact: The name comes from the Latin 'lavare', meaning 'to wash'. The Romans scented their baths with lavender.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A towering tree that cloaks itself in clouds of trumpet-shaped lilac-blue flowers. When the blossoms fall, they carpet streets and lawns in purple.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late spring to early summer in the Northern Hemisphere (May to June), notably in warm regions where it is grown as a street tree
plants.location: Warm regions such as southern California and Arizona in the USA, where it is widely planted as a street tree
plants.funFact: Jacaranda is native to South America, yet it is best known for its blooms in distant cities. Its spectacular show comes without leaves in some regions, as the flowers often appear before the new foliage.
